prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state, and for its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B048 as my preferred configuration, but after the first-round exchange I hold it with a narrower claim than in round 1. What the committee can defend is a discovery with a clear conceptual origin and a decisive experimental confirmation. Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal-invariant band insulators fall into a Z2 class with protected helical edge states and no magnetic field, and Molenkamp's group measured the predicted quantized edge conductance in HgTe wells. Two decades of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and scanning probes, and spread into photonic, mechanical and cold-atom systems, make it mature. It also differs from the 2016 prize: Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz concerned quantum Hall topology and defect-driven transitions with broken time-reversal symmetry, not Z2 matter protected by time-reversal symmetry. I place weight on this because breadth of support across the room is evidence that the science travels across subfields, but I do not treat a support count as a substitute for the argument. If the argument fails on attribution, the count should not rescue it.
statement.case_against: The chair's point is the strongest objection and I no longer think it can be answered by wording alone. Molenkamp tested the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, not the Kane-Mele graphene model, whose spin-orbit gap is tiny. A citation therefore credits a concept (Kane and Mele) and an experiment (Molenkamp) joined by a step that the three names omit. The three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hasan and Cava) is also outside the names. My answer is that the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state are the conceptual discovery and BHZ is a materials-specific realisation within it, but this is a priority judgement and reasonable members can reverse it. The disqualifying omission would be a citation that implied BHZ or the 3D materials were credited. The overlap with the 2016 prize is conceptual rather than fatal, but it is a real cost to the committee's balance.

responses.point: Pearce argues that Molenkamp's HgTe experiment tested the BHZ prediction, not Kane and Mele's graphene proposal, so a three-name B048 credits a theory and an experiment that do not connect directly, and moves B016 ahead because its chain from Bistritzer-MacDonald to Jarillo-Herrero is direct.
responses.response: This is the sharpest form of the attribution objection and I concede the factual core: the HgTe experiment was designed around BHZ. I still do not think the link to Kane and Mele is absent, because the Z2 classification and the helical edge-state concept are what BHZ and the experiment instantiate, and the conductance measured in HgTe is the signature Kane and Mele predicted. But I accept that the chain is less direct than in B016 and that this is B048's real defect. Where I differ is on the size of B016's advantage: its chain is direct, yet the pairing mechanism is unsettled and Cao and the co-first authors fall outside the names. I weigh that as a comparable gap of a different kind, so I do not move, but B016 stays my first alternative.

responses.point: Danielsson offers to rework the allocation if I can show that BHZ was more than a materials recipe, but notes that the three-person ceiling means one of Kane, Mele or Molenkamp would have to give way.
responses.response: I will not argue that BHZ was only a recipe. It identified the inverted-band HgTe system, and without it the experiment would not have been targeted. My claim is narrower: BHZ is built on the Kane-Mele Z2 framework and the quantum spin Hall concept, so a citation that names the Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state, and its first observation in HgTe, is accurate without crediting BHZ. I agree that no one of the three should give way, since removing Kane, Mele or Molenkamp would strip either the concept or the confirmation. The committee should state openly that BHZ and the 3D work lie outside the prize and decide whether that is acceptable.

responses.point: Lindroth treats the BHZ question as one that must be answered before B048 goes ahead of the clock prize, and says the lattice-clock credit is cleaner, with the overlap with 2016 conceptual rather than fatal.
responses.response: I accept that B049 has the cleaner credit and I raised no objection on maturity. My remaining hesitation is only about novelty, whether the lattice clock is a new principle or the best realisation of the comb and ion-control tool kit after 2005 and 2012. Her description of the magic-wavelength trapping as a new principle that permits many-atom interrogation is persuasive to me as an outsider, and it is why I now list B049 as an alternative. Where I differ is that a clean credit is not enough to decide the matter if the discovery is judged incremental. I would want her and Kroll to say whether Katori's priority over other early lattice-clock proposers is documented in the record, and I cannot settle that.

responses.point: Eriksson placed B016 first because the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero experiment are directly linked, but accepts that maturity favours topological insulators and would not strongly resist B048.
responses.response: I agree that B016 is the strongest case on direct theory-to-experiment linkage and I agree that the committee is divided between B016 and B048 rather than behind one. On the maturity question I would not wait on B016 for the superconducting mechanism alone, and I would restrict its citation to the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states. Our difference is how to weigh seven years of confirmation against a credit chain that breaks at BHZ. I prefer the longer confirmation record, while recognising that a member who weighs credit more heavily will reach the other answer.

uncertainties: Whether a citation worded around the Z2 state and its first observation in HgTe leaves BHZ and the 3D topological insulator work fairly outside the prize, or whether that omission makes the prize unsound; I rely on recalled history that I have not verified here.
Whether the conceptual overlap with the 2016 prize should lower B048 relative to B016 and B049.
Whether seven years of confirmation and an open pairing mechanism make B016 premature, or whether its direct theory-to-experiment chain makes it the safer configuration.
Whether Katori's priority among early lattice-clock proposers is secure enough to rely on for B049.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen from the first-round exchange. I have no documented connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori or Ye. My neighbouring interest in statistical mechanics, topological defects and B041 is scientific, and I no longer carry B041 into the final position because no other member supports it.
